rationale:
**Confirmation:** the assessments disagreed

First assessment `true`: No gap in the `{cite}` of `requirements.authoring.usage_storage` on `src/authoring/usage.rs#struct[UsageLog]`.

- **Not a test.** `UsageLog` is a plain struct.
- **No `{impl}` needed.** `UsageLog` is not a root of the requirement's implementation. Several items already marked `{impl}` for `requirements.authoring.usage_storage` use it, and a reviewer reaches it by following them. These items are `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[prepare_assessment]`, `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[PendingAssessment]/fn[failed]` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[PendingAssessment]/fn[persisted]`. The record's serialized form is constrained by `src/authoring/usage.rs#struct[UsageRecord]`, not by `UsageLog`, because `UsageLog` is not `Serialize`.
- **The `{cite}` is appropriate.** `UsageLog` holds the usage record (`record`), the location of the per-run JSON file under the state root (`path`), and the start `Instant` used for the elapsed and end times. A change to the requirement's record location, filename or contents could require changing this struct. It relies on that behavior without implementing it.
- **No redundancy.** `UsageLog` has no `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the same requirement.

Second assessment `false`: The `{cite}` of `requirements.authoring.usage_storage` on `src/authoring/usage.rs#struct[UsageLog]` is a gap.

- **Not an {impl} root.** `UsageLog` is reached from items that already carry `{impl}` for this requirement. Those items are `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[author_evidence_with_output]`, `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[prepare_assessment]`, `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[PendingAssessment]/fn[failed]` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[PendingAssessment]/fn[persisted]`. `prepare_assessment` calls `UsageLog::start`, `save`, `finish` and the other methods, and `failed` and `persisted` call `finish`. Code a reviewer reaches through a marked item needs no reference, so no `{impl}` is called for.
- **Not a test.** It is a plain struct.
- **The cite is not supported by the item's own code.** The struct has four fields: `record: UsageRecord`, `path: PathBuf`, `started: Instant` and a `first_conversation_finished` callback. None of them is a field list, serialized form, format version, outcome value or path layout that the requirement defines. The requirement's record fields live in `UsageRecord` (`src/authoring/usage.rs#struct[UsageRecord]`), which is the `#[derive(Serialize)]` type. The path layout and the `<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` computation live in `UsageLog::start` and `save`. A change to the requirement's text would change those items, not the field set of `UsageLog`. The `started` timer and the callback have nothing to do with the requirement.

The item therefore does not need a reference to `requirements.authoring.usage_storage`.

Recorded the second assessment (`false`).

text: Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
